stocks.discussion_driver: Deutsche Bank downgraded Dollar General to Hold from Buy and slashed its price target to $110 from $170, citing persistent weakness in core low-income consumer spending and a widening K-shaped economy gap. The stock has shed ~33% from its 52-week high and faces a critical earnings report on June 2, with investors cautious ahead of a late-May shareholder vote as well.
bull_case: Deep value at ~15x trailing P/E and ~2.3% dividend yield; stock trades 37% below the Wall Street consensus target of $144, with 10 buy-rated analysts still on the Street despite the Deutsche Bank downgrade
New CEO brings fresh operational focus that could drive same-store sales recovery and margin improvement, especially as current consumer headwinds from inflation and tariffs eventually ease
bear_case: Core low-income customer base continues to face macro pressure; Deutsche Bank and others cite a structurally widening K-shaped economy gap that limits same-store sales growth near term
Elevated earnings risk heading into June 2 results with the stock sliding ahead of the print; competitive pressure from Walmart, Amazon, and Dollar Tree remains intense

stocks.discussion_driver: Bank of America resumed coverage on Workday with a Neutral rating and $140 price target, citing valuation concerns and slowing enterprise software spending — a fresh headwind even after WDAY's solid Q1 FY2027 earnings on May 21 (revenue +14% YoY to $2.54B, EPS beat of $2.66 vs $2.51 estimate). The stock is down ~52% from its 52-week high and trades with an RSI of 27.64, deep in oversold territory.
bull_case: Q1 FY2027 results beat on both top and bottom lines; total subscription backlog of $27.3B (up 10.9% YoY) provides strong multi-year revenue visibility and underpins durable cash flow

RSI of 27.64 signals deeply oversold conditions, with 47.6% upside to analyst consensus target of $183.75; any stabilization in enterprise IT budgets or multiple re-rating could catalyze a sharp recovery
bear_case: Valuation remains stretched at 93.5x trailing P/E even after the steep selloff; multiple expansion is unlikely amid slowing enterprise software spending and increasing margin scrutiny
Growing chorus of analyst caution — BofA Neutral ($140 PT), Goldman Sachs Neutral ($206 PT), and numerous other target cuts — signals fading institutional conviction and limited near-term catalysts
sources: Bank of America via Seeking Alpha
